Trigger: `D` (rebindable; menu + context menu), result overlaid where the detailed info panel goes; optional auto-describe when the user PARKS on an image >500 ms (EAGER_PREP_DELAY pattern) — cancelled on advance (generation counter), results cached RAM-only per image (meta_cache pattern), dropped on exit. Two backends behind one core-owned seam/policy: (1) macOS 27+ Foundation Models framework (on-device, image input, ships with the OS); (2) an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint (LM Studio / llama.cpp / Ollama — Qwen3-VL-8B or 27B-class on an RTX 5090) for Windows and power users. One-shot v1 (streaming later if slow; expected 1–5 s). Prompt built in core so both backends match: salient EXIF (capture time, camera/lens, raw GPS coords — offline reverse-geocoder is a LATER upgrade), filename + parent folder; all context framed as UNVERIFIED (trust-the-pixels instruction — hallucination guard) with epoch-default junk dates filtered out. New 'AI Descriptions' settings section (own tab on macOS): backend picker (Auto/Apple/Local), endpoint URL + model, auto-describe toggle, speak-aloud toggle. Interim HUD note: pb-hud font fallback helps the current paragraph renderer and non-Latin EXIF/text values, but task #54 makes Description/Ask a rich panel with selectable/copyable text; the HUD is not the final rich-text surface. Additions from final discussion: 'Speak descriptions' is ALSO a menu toggle (Image menu, Mute-Live-Photo-Audio pattern, MenuState checkbox); the AI Descriptions settings section carries a short privacy blurb (custom endpoint = your images upload to that URL, incl. auto-describe — keep it local/trusted; online services may retain/train on images). || WWDC26 CONFIRMED (2026-07-04, https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2026/241/): FM image input is NEW in the 2026 release (macOS 27) — on-device, ships with the OS, no download/setup; API is session.respond { PROMPT; Attachment(x) } where x = NSImage/CGImage/CIImage/CVPixelBuffer/file-URL, any size/aspect. tasks.title: Vendor-patch wgpu-hal: presentsWithTransaction during window-mode transitions (flash-free resize, MTKView-grade)
tasks.description: Make the fullscreen-toggle / resize composite pixel-perfect on macOS. Today's mitigation (2026-07-04) is benign-not-atomic: layerContentsPlacement=.center + contentsGravity on the canvas view means the one racy composite ({new bounds, previous drawable} — wgpu presents out-of-band from the CA transaction that moves the bounds) shows UNSCALED stale content for <=1 frame instead of a stretch. The atomic fix is Apple's presentsWithTransaction (what MTKView flips on during live resize). wgpu-hal 22's Metal backend ALREADY implements the correct present branch (Surface.present_with_transaction pub field; present does commit -> wait_until_scheduled -> drawable.present(); the field's own doc comment cites resize-sensitive UI apps) — but wgpu 22 gives no safe way to SET it: Surface::as_hal hands out only a shared ref, there's no creation-time knob, and configure() re-asserts the flag onto the layer every resize (so flipping the CAMetalLayer property from Swift is useless). PLAN: (1) vendor wgpu-hal 22.0 with a ~20-line patch — interior-mutable flag (AtomicBool) + set_present_with_transaction(&self) — wired via [patch.crates-io] like the sevenz-rust2 precedent; (2) pb-render seam Renderer::set_present_with_transaction(bool) reaching the hal surface through Surface::as_hal; (3) flip it ON only around window-mode transitions (and optionally during live resize), OFF otherwise — presentsWithTransaction costs a main-thread waitUntilScheduled block per present, which MTKView itself only tolerates while resizing; the photo hot path (hold-to-blaze) never resizes, keypress->photon untouched; (4) owner drives the upstream PR against wgpu trunk — NOTE trunk's Metal backend was rewritten on objc2 in 23+, so the trunk patch is the same concept but different code; a hal-level setter is the least-bikesheddable API shape. When the eventual egui/wgpu upgrade train moves off 22, the vendored patch drops (if merged) or re-rolls. Payoff is polish: the remaining <=1-frame unscaled reveal on F-toggles/live-resize becomes zero-artifact.

Prior art: vertical-only *user*-resizing was PUNTED after 5 failed attempts (see git history + the comment above the TabView, and the ns2-native-dialogs memory); this is the different goal of auto-fit-to-content, not user-resize.
tasks.details: Approach to try (needs ON-DEVICE iteration — SwiftUI window sizing can't be verified headlessly): the Settings scene already uses .windowResizability(.contentSize), so per-tab fixed frames are what pin the size. Options: (a) drop the fixed heights and let contentSize follow each Form's natural height — historically the Forms expanded to fill instead of reporting intrinsic height, which is likely why it failed; (b) measure each pane's content height (onGeometryChange on the Form's content, guard against feedback loops) and apply it as the frame height; (c) keep fixed frames but compute them from the content once at build. Watch for: the object_setClass/KVO segfault hazard on SwiftUI windows (never do that); jumpy resize when switching tabs; the window collapsing to min. tasks.title: Smoother hold-to-pan / hold-to-zoom — gentler acceleration curve
tasks.description: Owner feel note (2026-07-09): holding the pan/zoom keys accelerates too aggressively and doesn't feel smooth — want a slower, gentler ramp with smoother motion. The hold-to-view loop is AppCore::apply_view_holds (crates/pb-app-core/src/app_core_impl.rs:5642), driven by the tuning constants in crates/pb-app-core/src/engine.rs: zoom e-folding rate ramps ZOOM_MIN_RATE 0.5 -> ZOOM_MAX_RATE 2.5 over ZOOM_RAMP_SECS 0.7 (exp() applied multiplicatively about center); pan speed ramps PAN_MIN_SPEED 450 -> PAN_MAX_SPEED 3200 px/s over PAN_RAMP_SECS 0.7. Both are already time-based (frame-rate independent, dt-clamped to 0.1s) so 'smoother' here means the FEEL of the ramp, not a timing bug. Two levers: (a) TUNING — lower the max rate/speed and/or lengthen the ramp so it starts and stays gentler (e.g. PAN_MAX ~1800-2400, ZOOM_MAX ~1.5-2.0, RAMP ~1.0-1.2s), a one-file constant change; (b) CURVE SHAPE — the ramp is currently LINEAR in t (min + (max-min)*(t/ramp)); an ease-in (smoothstep / t^2) keeps fine control longer at the start before building speed, which reads as 'smoother'. Optional stretch: a short release ease-out / inertia so motion doesn't stop dead on key-up. Shared-core feel change (helps macOS + Linux too), surfaced while testing on Windows; keep it a measured, owner-in-the-loop tuning pass, not a blind edit.

(2) Swap the linear ramp for an ease-in in apply_view_holds: factor the shared 'min + (max-min) * shape(t/ramp)' into a small pure helper (e.g. ease_in(u)=u*u or smoothstep) so zoom and pan share one curve and it's unit-testable (assert monotonic, ease_in(0)=0, ease_in(1)=1, gentler-than-linear midpoint). Keep the multiplicative exp() zoom-about-center and the pan clamp untouched. (3) Optional inertia: on key release, decay the last velocity over ~150-250ms instead of zeroing zoom_started/pan_started immediately — bigger change, own subtask, only if the owner still wants more polish after (1)+(2). Note the scroll-wheel/trackpad steps (WHEEL_ZOOM_STEP, PIXEL_ZOOM_STEP, WHEEL_PAN_STEP, PINCH_GAIN) are a SEPARATE input path (AppCore::scroll, not apply_view_holds) — the owner's note is about held-key motion, so leave the gesture constants unless they ask. Prime directive: this is off the photo hot path (only runs while a pan/zoom key is held), so feel is free to change; still no per-frame heap alloc. Consider whether any of these should become settings (nav ramp/start/max are already configurable) vs hard-coded; default to constants unless the owner wants a knob.

tasks.title: Cursor auto-hide option — hide the mouse pointer when idle / in speed mode (all platforms)
tasks.description: Owner ask (2026-07-09): let the mouse pointer hide, as an OPTION, on every platform where possible. Half the plumbing already exists but nothing actually hides today: contract::CursorKind::Hidden is defined (crates/pb-app-core/src/contract.rs:80) and its doc even claims 'the viewer hides the cursor in the chrome-free hot path and restores it on movement' — but (1) NOTHING in the core emits SetCursor(Hidden) (hover_cursor at app_core_impl.rs:2678-2686 only emits Grab/Grabbing/Pointer/Default), (2) the winit shell STUBS it: cursor_icon maps Hidden -> CursorIcon::Default (crates/pb-app/src/main.rs:3361, with the note 'Hidden is unused on the SetCursor path'), so Windows/Linux never hide, and (3) only the macOS shell honors it (CoreModel.swift:1897 NSCursor.setHiddenUntilMouseMoves(true)) — and even that is dead code since the core never sends it. So this is: wire a core auto-hide POLICY, make the winit shell truly hide, confirm macOS, and expose it as a setting. 'Where possible': winit uses Window::set_cursor_visible(false) (works on Windows + X11; on Wayland cursor visibility is compositor-mediated and may be a soft no-op — accept graceful degradation there).
tasks.details: Design: (a) POLICY in core — after N seconds with no CursorMoved (and no panel/dialog/menu open, and pointer not over a clickable affordance), emit CoreEffect::SetCursor(CursorKind::Hidden); any real pointer movement restores the resolved cursor (Default/Grab/etc via the existing hover_cursor path). Drive the timeout off the existing tick-deadline machinery (next_deadline / self.now) — do NOT add a spin; the app already sleeps when idle, so schedule a wake at the hide deadline. A natural stronger default: in the borderless Fullscreen 'speed mode' (WindowMode::Fullscreen) hide sooner or immediately-on-idle, since that mode is the chrome-free hot path the contract doc references. (b) WINIT SHELL — replace the Hidden->Default stub: on SetCursor(Hidden) call window.set_cursor_visible(false); on any other kind restore visibility + set the icon. Track visibility so we don't thrash set_cursor_visible every event. Windows + X11 honor it; Wayland may ignore — that's the 'where possible' caveat, log/accept. (c) macOS — the core now actually emits Hidden; verify setHiddenUntilMouseMoves gives the desired feel, or switch to explicit NSCursor.hide()/unhide() (persistent hide with our own restore-on-move) if the until-mouse-moves auto-restore fights the policy. (d) SETTING — add a serde-default bool (e.g. settings.hide_cursor_when_idle, maybe an idle-seconds too) and surface a toggle in BOTH shells (egui Settings General/Appearance tab via a pb-ui toggle_with_label + the SwiftUI SettingsView), defaulting per owner (likely ON in fullscreen, or a simple global ON/OFF). Privacy #2: cursor state is ephemeral runtime state; the only persisted bit is the toggle in settings.toml — no viewing trace. Keep the policy pure/testable in pb-app-core (feed it 'now' + last-move time + mode + overlay state, assert it emits Hidden after the timeout and restores on move) so it isn't a shell-only behavior.
tasks.testStrategy: Pure: unit-test the idle policy in pb-app-core — given last-move time, now, window mode, and whether an overlay/affordance is active, assert it decides Hidden after the timeout and Restore on movement, and never hides while a dialog/menu/hover-affordance is up. Manual per platform: Windows (winit) — leave the pointer still over a photo, confirm it vanishes after the timeout and reappears on the first move; confirm it does NOT hide while hovering the Cancel-scan chip or with a panel/menu open; confirm it hides sooner/at-idle in fullscreen speed mode. macOS — same feel via the SwiftUI shell. Linux — X11 hides; note Wayland behavior. Settings: toggling the option OFF disables all hiding on every platform; the setting round-trips through settings.toml (and the SwiftUI FFI) and nothing else is persisted.

tasks.title: Resolve LGPL static-link compliance (libheif/libde265 + FFmpeg) before public/commercial release
tasks.description:
The Windows binary statically links libheif + libde265, both LGPL-3.0. LGPL requires that users can relink the application against a modified version of the library - a static link alone does not satisfy this. Flagged in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md during the task #76 license audit (dav1d itself is BSD-2 and fully handled by the notices file; Linux AppImage bundles shared .so files so it already complies). Not urgent while the app is private/free, but a MUST before any public or commercial release (Velopack commercial plan).

CROSS-REF (2026-07-14, task #100): if #100 lands, FFmpeg (LGPL-2.1, no --enable-gpl) joins libheif/libde265 under this same obligation. Solve the relink story ONCE for all three rather than for libheif alone — #100.6 is written to defer to whatever this task decides. Do not close #77 with a libheif-only remedy without checking #100's status first.

=== UPDATE 2026-07-14: #100 HAS LANDED. This is no longer conditional. ===
Windows now statically links THREE LGPL libraries, not two: libheif 1.23.0 + libde265 1.1.1 (LGPL-3.0-or-later, §4) and FFmpeg 8.1.2 (LGPL-2.1-or-later, §6 — vcpkg's own copyright file confirms LGPL-2.1; gpl/nonfree features are opt-in and off). FFmpeg's role on Windows is narrow (demux/metadata only; MF still does 100% of decode) but that is IRRELEVANT to the obligation — LGPL attaches to distribution and linkage, not to how much of the library is called. dav1d stays fine (BSD-2-Clause, attribution only, already handled).

A SHIPPED-DOC DEFECT was found and fixed while reviewing this (2026-07-14). THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is copied into the Velopack package by release-windows.ps1:158 — i.e. it ships next to the exe as the user-facing legal notice — and it stated "**Windows does not use FFmpeg** (Media Foundation handles video there)". .taskmaster/docs/ffmpeg-compliance.md said the same, and its entire argument rested on it. Both were true when written and were made false by #100. A Windows build cut in that window would have distributed FFmpeg under notices affirmatively denying it — materially worse than a documented open item. Both docs + CLAUDE.md's Licensing section now state the Windows static link and flag it. The underlying obligation is unchanged; only the honesty of the paperwork was restored.

THE DECISION (owner): DLL linkage vs static + published relink materials.
* DLL (LGPL-2.1 §6(b) / LGPL-3.0 §4(d)(1)) — the conventional answer, already what macOS and Linux do, so it makes all three platforms tell one story. Cost: vcpkg dynamic triplet (x64-windows / arm64-windows) instead of *-windows-static-md; ffmpeg-sys-next then wants VCPKGRS_DYNAMIC=1 (the exact knob the `static` feature was added to defeat — see #100.1); build.rs changes; ~7 DLLs to stage, sign (Azure Trusted Signing) and ship per arch. NOT YET MEASURED: install size almost certainly grows — the +3.06 MB static figure exists because the linker discards every unreferenced object, and a DLL exports everything. That measurement should precede the call.
* Static + relink materials (LGPL-2.1 §6(a) / LGPL-3.0 §4(d)(0)) — legally recognized, and it keeps the small binary, but it requires publishing PhotoBlaze's OWN object files per release so a user can relink against a modified library. Object code, not source, so the proprietary position survives — but it is per-release, toolchain-specific plumbing that most vendors avoid for exactly that reason.
RECOMMENDATION: DLL. Measure the size delta first so the call is made on numbers.

=== MEASURED 2026-07-14 — the size objection to DLLs is DEAD (+0.8 MB). ===
Built the whole native stack against vcpkg's DYNAMIC x64-windows triplet (libheif[core], dav1d, ffmpeg with the SAME demux-only portfile trim) and compared like for like:
  STATIC  (ships today): exe 35.07 MB                       = 35.07 MB
  DYNAMIC (LGPL remedy): exe 29.04 MB + 7 DLLs 6.82 MB      = 35.87 MB
  DELTA: +0.80 MB (+2.3%) on-disk payload.
The going-in fear was a 10-15 MB regression, reasoning that a DLL exports everything while a static link lets the linker discard unreferenced objects. That reasoning was WRONG at this scale: the exe shrank 6.03 MB and the DLLs only weigh 6.82 MB back. Do not re-litigate this from intuition.

The DLLs (transitive closure of the real import table via dumpbin, not a guess): avcodec-62 1.94, dav1d 1.70, heif 1.33, avutil 0.84, avformat 0.54, libde265 0.35, swresample-6 0.12. NOTE swscale-9.dll is NOT needed — Windows only reads containers, so the scaler is never imported. VERIFIED RUNNING: photoblaze.exe copied to an empty dir with exactly those 7 DLLs starts and reports its version, so the set is complete (nothing is dlopen'd behind dumpbin's back — libheif's plugin loader is already OFF via the portfile patch).

HOW IT WAS BUILT (the seam is committed and inert by default):
* pb-decode/build.rs takes PB_VCPKG_DYNAMIC=1 -> the plain x64-windows / arm64-windows triplet and dylib= link kinds. Unset = today's static behaviour, byte for byte.
* FFmpeg additionally needs VCPKGRS_DYNAMIC=1 in the env. It does NOT need the ffmpeg-next 'static' feature removed: ffmpeg-sys-next only SETS that var when 'static' is off (build.rs:700-706) and never unsets it, so an externally-set value survives and the vcpkg crate honours it. That is why the whole spike flips on two env vars with no Cargo.toml edit — worth knowing, since #100.1 added 'static' specifically to defeat that variable.

STILL TO DO for a real DLL ship (none of it measured yet): setup-libheif.ps1 installs the dynamic triplet; release-windows.ps1 stages the 7 DLLs into $Stage and signs them (Azure Trusted Signing) alongside the exe; CI lanes; arm64. dav1d is BSD-2 so it could stay static, but one triplet supplies the tree — splitting it buys ~1.7 MB of DLL for extra build complexity, probably not worth it.

=== IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-14: Windows now links the LGPL libraries as DLLs by default. ===
The three obligations turned out to be INDEPENDENT, and all three are now addressed:
  1. LINKAGE (LGPL-2.1 6(b) / LGPL-3.0 4(d)(1)) - the default flipped to DLLs. build.rs
     `vcpkg_dynamic()` is now dynamic-by-default with `PB_VCPKG_STATIC=1` as the A/B escape
     hatch (the spike's polarity was the reverse: PB_VCPKG_DYNAMIC=1 opted IN). A
     PB_VCPKG_STATIC=1 build is the non-compliant configuration by definition and must never ship.
  2. LICENSE TEXT (LGPL-2.1 6 / LGPL-3.0 4(b)) - `licenses/` ships verbatim COPYING files for
     libheif, libde265, FFmpeg (LGPLv2.1) and dav1d, staged into the Velopack package, the macOS
     .app (Contents/Resources/licenses) and the AppImage (usr/share/licenses). This was MISSING ON
     EVERY PLATFORM and was the most exposed item: unlike the static link (which had 6(a) as a
     fallback defence), shipping without the licence text has no defence at all.
  3. ATTRIBUTION (LGPL-3.0 4(c)) - triggered only because About displays a copyright line; the
     About card now names each bundled library + its copyright and points at the licences folder.

FFmpeg follows the switch WITHOUT an env var: pb-decode's `ffmpeg-next` dep no longer enables the
`static` feature, and ffmpeg-sys-next sets VCPKGRS_DYNAMIC=1 itself exactly when `static` is absent.
Re-adding `features = ["static"]` there silently returns FFmpeg to a non-compliant static link -
Cargo.toml carries a warning comment saying so.

TWO TRAPS FOUND WHILE WIRING IT (both cost real time, both now handled + documented):
* libde265's import lib is `de265.lib` but its static lib is `libde265.lib` - the vcpkg triplets
  disagree on that ONE name (heif.lib and dav1d.lib are stable across both, and the DLL is still
  libde265.dll). A `dylib=libde265` link name gives LNK1181. The link name must track the triplet,
  not just the link kind.
* `Enter-VsDevShell` OVERWRITES VCPKG_ROOT with the vcpkg bundled inside Visual Studio - a tree with
  none of our pinned ports - even when the caller exported the right value first. Since ffprobe
  needs a Developer shell (bindgen), EVERY shipped build passes through this. scripts/vs-dev-env.ps1
  now captures VCPKG_ROOT and restores it (falling back to ~/vcpkg like build.rs does, because
  ffmpeg-sys-next has no such fallback and would otherwise hunt for FFmpeg in the VS tree).

Also: build.rs copies the vcpkg DLLs into target/<profile>/ AND target/<profile>/deps/ (Windows
resolves from the executable's own directory, and cargo puts tests in deps/), so `cargo run`/`cargo
test` work with no PATH dance and the shipped DLL set is the one the tests ran against.

REMAINING before this can be closed:
* ARM64 is UNVERIFIED end to end (no ARM64 box) - the dynamic triplet, the de265.lib naming and the
  DLL staging are all x64-measured only.
* No release has actually been cut with the DLL config yet; release-windows.ps1 stages the DLLs via a
  dumpbin transitive import walk and signs them, but that path is untested against a real `vpk pack`.
* The `cargo license` sweep of the rest of the dependency tree (per this task's details) is still not
  done.

=== VALIDATED 2026-07-14/15 (ARM64) — the last linkage blocker is CLOSED. ===
The 0.2.1 win-arm64 release was cut and PUBLISHED with the DLL config on a real ARM64 box, closing
the "ARM64 is UNVERIFIED end to end (no ARM64 box)" item above. Evidence from the shipped package:
* setup-libheif.ps1 -Triplet arm64-windows built the DLL triplet cleanly (libheif 1.23.0, libde265
  1.1.1, dav1d 1.5.3, ffmpeg 8.1.2). The de265.lib-vs-libde265.lib naming trap did NOT bite on
  arm64 — build.rs's triplet-tracking link name is correct there too.
* dumpbin /dependents on the PACKAGED blazeviewer.exe shows heif.dll, dav1d.dll, avcodec-62.dll,
  avformat-62.dll, avutil-60.dll in the import table (libde265.dll arrives via heif.dll's own
  imports; swresample-6 via avcodec/avformat) => dynamic linkage CONFIRMED IN THE ARTIFACT, not
  just in the script. swscale-9 correctly ABSENT, matching the x64 measurement exactly.
* licenses/ + THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md ship in the package payload beside the exe; Setup.exe is
  Authenticode Valid (FullSpec Systems). Feed published as channel win-arm64 and verified live;
  /latest/win-arm64 Caddy redirect added.

ARM64 TOOLCHAIN NOTE (cost hours, not obvious): --features ffprobe needs libclang for bindgen at
<BuildTools>\VC\Tools\Llvm\ARM64\bin — the VS 'C++ Clang tools for Windows' component. The quiet
vs_installer CLI CANNOT install it: non-elevated --quiet exits 5007 ('commands with --quiet should
be run elevated from the beginning'), and even elevated it dies in ~7s on a temp-cache lock ('being
used by another process' — AV scanning the installer temp files). Use the VS Installer GUI ->
Modify -> Individual components -> 'C++ Clang tools for Windows'. AFTER installing, WAIT for
setup.exe to fully exit: vswhere -requires returns EMPTY while it finalizes, surfacing as
vs-dev-env.ps1's misleading 'No usable VS C++ install found ... Checked: (none)' even though
libclang.dll already exists on disk.

SHIPPED-DOC DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (2026-07-15). THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md had gone stale in the
OPPOSITE direction from the earlier #100 defect: it still declared libheif/libde265/dav1d/FFmpeg
'statically linked on Windows', flagged the relink condition as 'OPEN — not satisfied by
attribution alone', said 'A public or commercial Windows build must not ship until #77 closes',
and still said 'PhotoBlaze'. All false since the DLL default landed — and it shipped that way in
BOTH the x64 and arm64 0.2.1 releases. Rewritten to describe the real per-platform linkage, the
dumpbin-computed DLL set, the PB_VCPKG_STATIC / ffmpeg-next 'static' never-ship warnings, and the
four obligations. While rewriting, a genuine GAP was closed: shipping the DLLs means distributing
the libraries in object form, triggering corresponding-source (LGPL-2.1 §4 / LGPL-3.0 §4 via
GPL-3.0 §6). The file only POINTED at upstream, which is neither an accompaniment nor a §3 written
offer; it now carries an explicit 3-year written offer (contact jd@jdlien.com — swap for a support@
address if one is set up). Cheap to honour: the libraries are unmodified upstream at pinned versions.

REMAINING: only the `cargo license` / `cargo about` sweep of the Rust dependency tree. Both linkage
validation items (x64, arm64) are now done.

tasks.title: CLI polish: clap, --help/--version, session-override flags, Windows console attach
tasks.description: Make PhotoBlaze a pleasant cross-platform CLI citizen for scripted launches. Today (main.rs:3406-3525): hand-rolled args, no --help/--version, unknown flags silently swallowed; release Windows builds are GUI-subsystem so nothing can print anyway. Decision (owner, 2026-07-11): use clap 4 (derive) - binary cost is a rounding error on this exe, parse time is launch-only, and it buys polished help/typo suggestions/value validation/completions for a low-usage feature. clap lives in pb-app ONLY (pb-app-core stays toml-only per NS0); the CLI parses into a plain LaunchOverrides struct the core consumes. Overrides NEVER persist to settings.toml (a scripted --dark --slideshow=5 launch must not rewrite the user's config).
tasks.details:
Order of operations in main(): (1) Velopack --veloapp-* intercept stays FIRST (update.rs:402); (2) Windows: AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS) + rebind stdout/stderr BEFORE parsing (clap's help/errors are invisible without it; known cosmetic PowerShell prompt-interleave wart is acceptable); (3) clap parse; (4) launch. Register the hidden dev flags (--hud-gallery, --egui-shot, --settings-shot, --light, --tab, --welcome, --metrics) as hide=true so clap doesn't error on them. Parse-error fallback: no console attached (double-click / file association) -> existing Message dialog instead of a silent exit; console -> normal stderr + exit 2. Flag set (long + short where sensible), all mapping to existing state per the 2026-07-11 survey: --fullscreen/-f, --windowed/-w (exist); --recursive/-r, --no-recursive (exist); --info/--no-info (settings.show_image_info); --details (Panels.inspector, the Shift+I inspector); --folders (folder_tree_open); --slideshow[=SECS] (slideshow + interval); --scale <fit|fill|original> (scale_mode); --theme <light|dark|system> (appearance_mode); --mute (mute_live_audio); --shuffle (NEW small feature: start nav in the precomputed pb-core shuffle order - randomness today is per-keypress, not a mode); --version (build.rs build-id stamp, same string as About). Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage/bad path (with stderr message when console attached). Docs: README CLI section; optional clap_complete completions later. Estimate: 1-2 focused days; the AttachConsole shim is the only fiddly part.

RESOLVED DECISIONS (owner Q&A, 2026-07-11, branch feat/cli-clap): (a) STRICTNESS = Mixed - clamp an out-of-range --slideshow=SECS into [0.1s,60s] (matches the runtime slider's own clamp); --fullscreen + --windowed together = last-one-wins (no clap conflict error); a NONEXISTENT positional path still errors (exit 2, stderr when console). Unknown flags / bad enum values keep clap's own exit 2. (b) EXTRAS beyond #78's set: ADD --start-at <N|name> (open at the Nth photo, 1-based, or a matching filename, instead of the first; wins over --shuffle's random start; filename match applied once the deferred scan resolves). RESERVE --new-window as a parse-accepted no-op now, so the future single-instance task #1 has its documented bypass seam and clap won't reject it later. --sort <name|date|size|random> is DEFERRED (owner: cool idea but do it as a coherent app-wide sort-order feature first, not a CLI-only bolt-on); do NOT parse-accept it yet. (c) --shuffle MECHANICS (trivial - reuses existing last_nav-steers-slideshow design, app_core_impl.rs:2550-2553 + 1054): set last_nav = Nav::Random at launch so the slideshow AND hold-to-blaze auto-advance in the precomputed random order; a DIRECTORY launch also does one random jump when the playlist resolves (start on a random photo); a SPECIFIC-FILE launch honors that file as the start (no random jump) but still sets last_nav=Random for a later slideshow. Manual Next/Prev (space/backspace) stay SEQUENTIAL and steer the slideshow back to sequential - the existing contract, matching the owner's ask (random slideshow advance + random dir-start, not random manual stepping). Flip to full mode later if wanted. (d) TDD: Cli->LaunchOverrides is a pure mapping unit-tested via Cli::try_parse_from([...]); --shuffle/--reverse/--start-at get pb-core/app-core tests. LaunchOverrides is a plain Option-field struct in pb-app-core (no clap dep); AppCore applies it, never persists. Docs: README CLI section + CHANGELOG (Added). Note: task ids were stringified by the adding commit; normalized #78 back to numeric per the tasks.json convention. (e) --reverse ADDED (owner, 2026-07-11): a direction seam over the four existing Nav variants, all routed through the launch last_nav (the slideshow + hold-to-blaze already advance via last_nav, app_core_impl.rs:1054, and toggle_slideshow does NOT reset it :5102). Mapping: neither flag=Forward, --reverse=Backward, --shuffle=Random, --shuffle+--reverse=RandomPrev (reverse shuffle - already the Shift+Enter/RandomPrev action, keymap.rs:499). Directory start position: --shuffle=random photo, --reverse=LAST photo (runway to play backward), default=first; a specific-file launch always honors the file; --start-at wins over both. Runtime discoverability stays CLI-only here - the 'tap Left/Backspace during a running slideshow to reverse' steer already works emergently (manual nav steers the slideshow) and will just be documented; a dedicated runtime reverse toggle/menu item is a possible future micro-task. (f) ARCHITECTURE REVISION (owner, 2026-07-11): macOS CLI parity is now wanted 'now-ish' (owner finishes/tests on a real Mac later), so the clap parser is extracted into a NEW shared LIB crate `pb-cli` (depends on pb-app-core + clap) instead of living inside the pb-app BINARY - a binary crate can't be a dependency, and pb-app-core must stay clap-free (NS0). pb-app depends on pb-cli; later pb-mac-ffi depends on pb-cli too and exposes one FFI entry that feeds Swift's CommandLine.arguments through the SAME parser. pb-cli is FFI-ready by design: parse_from(args-iterator) -> Result<Cli, clap::Error> with NO process::exit (help/version/errors are clap::Error kinds each shell renders itself - which also serves the Windows AttachConsole + no-console Message-dialog fallback), and argv is always a parameter (never std::env inside the lib). The render-and-exit dev commands (--hud-gallery/--egui-shot/--settings-shot + --light/--tab/--welcome) STAY intercepted in pb-app before clap (as today), so the shared Cli holds only the real cross-platform flags (+ hidden --metrics). LaunchOverrides + launch_nav + apply_to_settings already landed in pb-app-core (green, 6 tests); Nav gained Debug.

tasks.details: PLAN (authoritative, rev 2 2026-07-12 - Codex review verified + incorporated): .taskmaster/plans/83-thumbnails-panel.md. Rev 2 key changes (all four P0s verified against the code): (1) the decode pool needs a MULTI-CONSUMER contract first - set_targets today replaces the whole want-set keyed by bare item index, so thumb demand could cancel viewer prefetch; request identity becomes {item, epoch, purpose, fit-class, tier} with one merged priority order (DisplayCurrent > DisplayPreview > DisplayFull > Poster > ThumbVisible > ThumbWarm > ThumbRefine) + an occupancy guard (thumb jobs capped at max(1, workers-2), expensive fills only while parked) + displacement tests. (2) T0 derivation = POST-UPLOAD BUFFER HANDOFF (neither event-loop resize nor pre-Outcome worker resize): after drain_results uploads to the ring, the CPU buffer moves over a bounded 2-3-slot channel to a dedicated derive thread - zero clone, zero display latency; derive_thumbnail contract covers RGBA8+ColorTransform (downscale then bake the 3x3+TRC), Rgba16F (fp16 downscale + extended-Reinhard tone-map + sRGB encode), straight alpha, never Nv12 (video = posters); corpus A/B perf gate (capture on/off, decode-to-upload + keypress->photon p50/p95/p99 unchanged) is the acceptance criterion. (3) T1 is FORMAT-GATED - zune JPEG ignores allow_preview and always full-decodes; explicit matrix: embedded-preview capable (RAW/HEIC/PSD/WIC), JPEG via kamadak-exif IFD1 thumbnail (small new work), full-decode fallback (parked-only, capped, cancellable - placeholders while flying are CORRECT), native scaled-decode = future T2, video = posters. (4) Playlist::jump_to ALREADY EXISTS (the #43 compare flip) - expose it, don't rebuild it; cold-jump instant present needs a dedicated TRANSIENT PREVIEW SLOT (non-ring, never evicts the ring; <=1MiB upload ~20us on the click pump, full decode replaces via the normal preview->full swap). P1s: exact-byte budgets per owner (canonical 256MB ~ 256 worst-case square thumbs, in-flight = channel cap, per-shell visible+overscan texture caches, fallible alloc degrades to placeholder - not 'OOM impossible'); deck+request generations with clear-on-delete/rebuild + preserve-on-append (matches rebuild_playlist convention); eviction classes pinned-visible > overscan > warm > rest; shell bridge = dirty counter + <=1 notification/pump + snapshot struct + per-entry pull-once accessor; FollowState as a pure tested state machine (programmatic-scroll generation distinguishes user scrolls). Owner-settled UX unchanged from rev 1: Thumbnails name, Shift+T, playlist order always, no keyboard focus, fixed uniform cells, THUMB_EDGE=512, linear strip (no wraparound ghosts), smooth<=2 viewports else snap, type badges only, rotation at draw, find-ready item-list-view seam.

tasks.description: Feasibility spike: point PhotoBlaze at a macOS Photos library (~/Pictures/Photos Library.photoslibrary) and browse it in-place — photos, videos, and Live Photos — without exporting first. subtasks.title: Subtitle stream + sidecar discovery
subtasks.description: DONE. SidecarOrigin (pb_decode::tracks: reopenable Path | ArchiveEntry{archive,entry} -- by NAME not index, since a .srt is not a library item) + TrackLocator::Sidecar. Naming rules + encodings in pb-app-core::sidecar (20 tests, pure). PhotoSource EXTENDED with sibling_names(i)/sibling_bytes(i,name) -- the only door to a non-library file: FsSource = read_dir the parent (bare-name-only, cannot escape the dir); ZipSource = the pooled handle's central directory, scoped to the item's archive folder both ways, same decompression-bomb guards as bytes(); ScopedSource delegates through the index map; SevenZSource DELIBERATELY reports none (solid+eager: an unindexed entry's bytes were never produced, so it would need a predicate change at open or a full re-decompress per read -- pinned by a test so the gap is a decision). Discovery merges into the catalog subtitles TrackSet in media_details::probe_job, continuing the catalog id namespace so a sidecar TrackId cannot collide with an embedded stream's. Design: pure over a LIST OF SIBLING NAMES (one impl serves both sources); ENUMERATES rather than chooses (a case-collision is just two tracks); case-insensitive BY RULE so a ZIP finds the same sidecars on every host. 29 pb-source tests, Windows cross-check clean.

subtasks.title: Decode text cues to timed plain text
subtasks.description: DONE 2026-07-15. BOTH tiers ship. Sidecars: SubRip + WebVTT parsed in pure Rust (cues.rs). EMBEDDED streams: pb_decode::ffmpeg::cues (ff_stream_subtitle_cues) demuxes + avcodec_decode_subtitle2 for MKV subrip/ass/webvtt and MP4 mov_text. Lives at the `ffprobe` level, NOT beside demux.rs (which is ffvideo-gated = absent on Windows): reading a subtitle stream needs a demuxer + a SUBTITLE decoder, never a video one, so the trimmed Windows FFmpeg serves it — resolving the #100.8 constraint (sidecars stay pure-Rust and never touch FFmpeg, so Windows' missing srt/webvtt/ass DEMUXER is moot; no need to widen the trim). KEY FACT: FFmpeg normalizes EVERY text decoder's output to one ASS envelope (ff_ass_get_dialog: 8 commas then Text), so text_cue::ass_event_text (pure, tested) is the only wire-format knowledge needed. STREAMING (the design that makes it usable): reading cues is a full linear pass over the container — MEASURED 39 s on the corpus MKV (4.4 GB over SMB) — because subtitle blocks are scattered through every cluster. As a blocking wait that is indistinguishable from broken. But the reader walks in presentation order at ~70x the rate playback consumes, so it hands cues over as it finds them: MEASURED first batch at 1.06 s, 177 batches, cancellation stops a read in ~1 s not 40. CueLoad::drop cancels, so a nav can't leave a worker chewing 20 GB. FUTURE OPT: the playback demuxer already reads these packets and discards them — forwarding them would make cues cost zero I/O, but it only exists on routes using OUR demuxer, and a feature must never be gated on a backend. Layer it under, never replace. TWO ffmpeg-next LANDMINES FOUND: (1) NO Drop for Subtitle and it never calls avsubtitle_free — leaks per cue unless you free it yourself; (2) Text::get/Ass::get are from_utf8_unchecked = UB on the non-UTF-8 payloads that really exist (CP1252 .srt muxed without sub_charenc). We read the C string lossily via raw ptr instead. MOJIBAKE REPAIR (pb_app_core::mojibake, 15 tests): the corpus MKV carries `â™ª` where `♪` belongs — VERIFIED with `ffprobe -show_data` to be IN THE FILE, not our bug. Undone only when provable: re-encode a run to CP1252, require the bytes be valid UTF-8. `café` fails that (E9 is a lead with no continuation) so it is untouched. Applied per-RUN, not whole-string, at the single choke point (CueTrack::from_cues) BOTH tiers pass through. ⚠ SAFE_LEADS excludes à/á on purpose: French 'voilà «' (E0 A0 AB) IS valid UTF-8 and a naive round-trip corrupts it into a Samaritan letter — pinned by a test. Cost: mojibake'd Thai/Devanagari stays broken; the right trade. Also needed the 5 WHATWG windows-1252 passthrough bytes (0x81/8D/8F/90/9D) — `”` is E2 80 9D, so without 0x9D every CLOSING curly quote stays broken while the opening one repairs. Found by a test, not the spec.

subtasks.description: UI SHIPPED (macOS) 2026-07-15 — owner-testing. All 8 axes are reachable: a 5th Settings tab (SubtitlesPane.swift, SF `captions.bubble`) over a LIVE PREVIEW. PERSISTENCE: SubtitleStyle gained serde + a nested Settings.subtitle_style. ⚠ #[serde(default)] on SubtitleStyle AND Shadow is load-bearing, not decoration: it lives BY VALUE (unlike Option<WindowGeometry>, which is absent-or-whole), so a partial [subtitle_style] table must fill gaps from Default — otherwise a hand-edited config setting one key fails to parse, and Settings::load's 'malformed -> defaults' rule DISCARDS EVERY OTHER SETTING IN THE FILE to punish one typo here. It uses the SAME rasterizer + to_params + place() as the real overlay, so it cannot drift — that IS the one-rasterizer decision paying off. Because it uses the real place(), dragging the vertical offset negative visibly walks the text into the letterbox (the owner's headline ask, unjudgeable otherwise). Backdrop = a 2.39:1 picture (dark->light gradient + a bright band, so white text crosses a hostile patch) in the user's real letterbox colour. ⚠ LAYOUT TRAP: the preview must NOT stretch to the full pane width — a swatch WIDER than 2.39:1 pillarboxes and shows NO bars, hiding the one setting it exists to explain (a first PNG dump at 760x300 did exactly that). Capped at 420pt, 16:9. Max width + line spacing sit behind a collapsed Advanced group so the pane fits the FIXED 560x680 window. FFI: SubtitleStyleFfi is its OWN flat form, deliberately not 28 more fields on the 37-field SettingsFormFfi — the preview needs the DRAFT style every slider tick, which would mean shipping all 65 fields per frame to redraw one swatch. Font picker = a curated shortlist (owner call: fontdb finds ~1114 faces, nearly all unusable as subtitles); the stored value is a NAME, so a full picker later invalidates nothing. BUGS FOUND WHILE BUILDING: (1) TOML can hold `nan` and f32::clamp PANICS on a NaN bound while a NaN input sails through it — non-finite is reset BEFORE any clamp. (2) to_params used the raw font_family, but the FFI can't carry Option<String> and sends "" for System. (3) Color->UInt8 must clamp first: a wide-gamut pick lands outside 0...1 in sRGB and UInt8(-3.0) TRAPS in Swift. (4) the preview spinner would have spun FOREVER — nothing re-renders SwiftUI when the 261 ms font worker lands, so a .task polls until ready. WINIT PRESENTER + SETTINGS SHIPPED 2026-07-16, owner-confirmed on screen ("Subtitles do display!") against a real film over SMB. Windows now reaches parity with macOS on the two things that matter: cues DRAW and the style is CONFIGURABLE.

WHAT LANDED
1. Renderer::set_subtitle_overlay (pb-render): a sixth overlay layer. Unlike every other overlay it is placed at an ABSOLUTE origin, not an inset from an edge -- the core already placed it (subtitle::place), the renderer only converts px -> NDC. y may be slightly negative BY DESIGN (place clamps the TEXT's box, so a soft shadow bleeds off the top rather than shoving the words down); the vertex helper takes f32 for exactly that.
2. ITS OWN PREMULTIPLIED BLEND PIPELINE -- the load-bearing find. pb_hud::subtitle emits premultiplied RGBA (its own tests enforce it); the other CPU overlays are authored straight and share a pipeline whose ALPHA_BLENDING multiplies by alpha. Sending one through the other multiplies TWICE and visibly darkens every antialiased edge: measured 0.108 vs 0.216 linear. A GPU readback test (`the_subtitle_pipeline_blends_premultiplied_not_straight`) fails on exactly that mistake -- verified by pointing it at the wrong pipeline. The value it asserts is also what the macOS CGImage .premultipliedLast path produces, so the two shells match by construction rather than by eye.
3. Drawn FIRST of the overlays (pass 1b), so chrome composites above: the toast that says "Subtitles: English" shares the bottom-center strip with the cue it is talking about.
4. The presenter is SHELL-LOCAL on purpose (App::present_subtitles), NOT in tick_subtitles. macOS draws the same bitmap as a SwiftUI overlay over its AVPlayerLayer; putting this in the shared tick would draw every cue twice there. One rasterizer, two presenters.
5. POST-MORTEM BUG #2, still live in this shell, now fixed: AppCore was built by struct literal with `subtitles: Default::default()` and never called SubtitleEngine::from_settings, so `subtitles = true` on disk launched with captions OFF. Latent only because there was no presenter to reveal it. VERIFIED by trace: first tick now reports on=true.
6. Settings > Subtitles tab (egui, #90.4): all eight axes over the live preview, mirroring SubtitlesPane.swift's grouping/bounds/copy. Binds SubtitleStyle as a struct (no FFI to flatten for) and needs no debounce (the existing fold coalesces a drag). The swatch borrows the app's ONE SubtitleRasterizer -- never a second FontSystem -- and caches its texture against the exact inputs it drew.
7. The native Windows menu had NO subtitle entry AT ALL (the 'View > Subtitles' item that looked like it existed is in menu_bar_spec = the LINUX egui bar). C/Shift+C both worked and nothing said so. Added Subtitles + Next Subtitle Track to the native View menu.

TWO BUGS FOUND BY LOOKING AT THE OUTPUT (the #90 rule, paying again)
- ui.available_width() is NOT a safe texture dimension: egui's first frame reports a default screen_rect, measured 4944pt -> a 9888px texture, and egui PANICS past the GPU limit rather than clamping. Capped at the device's real max_texture_side.
- Scaled controls must write back only on .changed(): round-tripping a fraction through x100 and /100 is not bit-exact (0.04 -> 0.040000001) and the settings fold saves on ANY diff, so writing back unconditionally spews a config write every frame the tab is merely open.

REMAINING (deliberately not attempted; both are #99, not #90.5)
- The winit TRACK PICKER UI. Core is ready and shell-agnostic (subtitle_picker_rows / select_subtitle_row / subtitle_tracks_known, incl. the tri-state). Two homes, both real work: the winit 'playback bar' is a hand-laid-out egui info pill (panels_ui.rs), not a transport HStack like the Mac's, so a popover means manual layout + hit-testing + the video_bar_interactive gate; and a menu flyout needs machinery muda lacks -- macOS uses NSMenuDelegate.menuNeedsUpdate to pull tracks as the menu opens, while muda builds the tree once and only mirrors checkmarks. Shift+C + the new menu item cover the function meanwhile.
- AUDIO TRACK SWITCHING ON WINDOWS. Blocked on more than effort: WasapiAudio::open takes no track at all, and the catalog hands out TrackLocator::FfStream (an FFMPEG stream index, since #100 made FFmpeg the demuxer) while MF's Source Reader enumerates its OWN indices -- a real currency mismatch the TrackLocator seam exists for but nobody has resolved. On top of that, Windows audio IS the master clock, so a mid-playback switch must tear down and re-prime it at the playhead (main.rs already documents this as the genuinely hard half). And it cannot be verified without listening. Left alone.

LINUX: unverified. Same wgpu path, so it should follow, but nobody has run it.

tasks.title: Feature-film poster frame selection on the Windows (MF) + macOS (AVFoundation) backends
tasks.description: The seek-deep, shallow-first, brightness+contrast poster selection (fixes all-black posters for films that open on a studio logo / fade-in) shipped only on the FFmpeg backend (crates/pb-decode/src/ffmpeg/poster.rs; Mac MKV/WebM + Linux). The Windows Media Foundation poster (mf_poster.rs) and the macOS AVFoundation poster (av_poster.rs, MP4/MOV via the Live-Photo streaming reader) still use the old first-non-black mean-luma walk (30 frames / ~1s), so feature-film posters remain black there. Port the same strategy: reuse the shared scoring (crate::video::poster_frame_score / POSTER_GOOD_SCORE / luma_stats_rgba8), add a head-walk then seek deeper (shallow-first offsets ~8/20/45/90s clamped to min(5min, 50%)) and pick the best-scoring frame. MF supports IMFSourceReader::SetCurrentPosition seeking; AVFoundation needs an AVAssetReader timeRange start offset added to the streaming reader (the harder one - the reader currently reads from the start). OWNER 2026-07-19: the Windows deep-walk (267b1e9b, on main) is flagged GOOD ENOUGH FOR NOW - the worst issue (pure-black posters) is resolved. Accepted quirk: some Netflix specials (e.g. Ali Wong) that previously showed good posters now pick white-ish frames - most likely the blank-title-card skip trading black leads for white cards; revisit only if it grates. The macOS AVFoundation half (subtask 2) remains open. DIAGNOSED 2026-07-19 (owner noticed thumb strip vs poster disagree on the same clip): the thumb strip and the main poster run the SAME scored walk (engine.rs Thumb-purpose videos route through the normal poster path) but at DIFFERENT decode fit sizes, and frames are scored AFTER fitting (mf_poster.rs ~288/~325 -> poster_frame_score ~384) against fixed thresholds (POSTER_DETAIL_MIN), so the gate is resolution-dependent: at display size the white title card's grain/vignette texture likely clears the detail gate (walk stops there); at thumb size downscaling averages it away, the card fails, and the walk continues to a real scene - hence thumb=scene, poster=white. Candidate fix when revisited: score every candidate on a fixed-size downscale (~256 px wide) so the pick is resolution-independent and thumb == poster by construction.

tasks.title: HDR HEIC preview-first on Windows (WIC reorder)
tasks.description: Task #18 finding #1 (Windows half). PQ/HLG HEICs bypass preview-first: wic.rs decode() returns the fp16 HDR full decode before the allow_preview thumbnail block, so HDR HEICs never get the fast SDR-thumbnail preview while scrolling. Fix: when allow_preview, try wic_decode_thumbnail FIRST (RGBA8, is_preview=true) regardless of HDR; only fall through to the is_hdr_transfer fp16 full when there is no thumbnail. The SDR8-preview -> fp16-full slot flip already works (upload_slot rebuilds the texture per call; drain_results upgrades a preview_resident item).
tasks.details: HDR capture is the iPhone default, so this is a growing class of photos. Verification harness gotchas: crates/pb-decode/examples/decode.rs hardcodes allow_preview=false (can't assert a preview) - use heic_bench or add a --preview mode reporting is_preview + PixelFormat. Confirm the test fixture actually has an nclx transfer 16/18 (an iPhone gain-map aux may not enter the PQ/HLG branch). Validate the WIC thumbnail's color: WIC exposes thumbnail retrieval and per-frame color contexts separately, so applying the primary image's colr to the thumbnail needs evidence, not assumption. Also make slot_bytes_estimate / VRAM planning fp16-aware if the sharp full-ring (prefetch_fulls, up to 8 workers) can leave the ring over budget after multiple 8 B/px upgrades (see #18.3).

tasks.title: Fill scale mode: cover-to-screen decode target (semantic Contain/Cover)
tasks.description: Task #18 finding #2. decode_fit() returns None for ScaleMode::Fill, so a 24MP HEIC in Fill decodes/uploads at full res though only a screen-sized cover crop shows. Fix with a SEMANTIC decode target (Contain vs Cover) computed per-image after each decoder knows its oriented dimensions - NOT a single current-dims cover box in decode_fit (that mis-sizes neighbors: a portrait neighbor of a landscape current gets 2x-upscaled and it sticks once resident).
tasks.details: Owner decision (2026-07-14): use the semantic Contain/Cover target despite ~40 FitBox construction sites across 3 crates - a mechanical change, preferable to shipping a known sharpness regression. downscale_to_fit currently uses min() (contain); Cover uses max(sw/w, sh/h) clamped to no-upscale, computed against each image's own dims, so the box can stay image-independent (the screen box) and neighbors are correct too. AUDIT ALL 9 decode_fit() consumers (not just prefetch + slot_bytes_estimate): it also drives video scaling/budgeting, animation decoding, Live Photo streaming, and macOS archive posters. Benefit for HEIC is upload/VRAM/CPU-downscale (finalize applies the box after a full decode), not decode time.

tasks.title: macOS HEIC/HDR preview-first (Image I/O embedded-thumbnail decode)
tasks.description: Task #18 finding #1 (macOS half). imageio.rs ImageIoDecoder::decode has NO thumbnail path and ignores allow_preview for ALL images (SDR and HDR) - so there is nothing to 'reorder' like the Windows WIC fix. Needs a real Image I/O embedded-thumbnail decode: CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex (embedded-only, so a missing thumbnail does NOT synthesize a full decode), with orientation + color-space handling, is_preview=true, and primary-dimension reporting; plus macOS compile + real-file preview/full-upgrade verification.
tasks.details: RATIONALE / IMPORTANCE (owner-requested, 2026-07-14): macOS HEIC preview-first is ENTIRELY ABSENT today - this is a NEW capability, not a regression fix. So Apple-Silicon users currently get no fast-scrub on HEIC/HDR libraries (every HEIC is a full decode on the scroll path). Importance: matters once the macOS build is a real shipping target; LOW URGENCY while Windows is the primary platform. subtasks.title: Encoded-byte cache in front of source.bytes()
subtasks.description: Every image decode calls source.bytes(item) (engine.rs:512), which for a ZIP re-inflates/re-reads the entry every call - so a resize (epoch bump -> re-decode) re-reads 39MB off SMB (~0.8s measured). Add a small bounded RAM-only LRU of encoded (inflated) bytes, consulted before source.bytes(). Kills the re-read for resize, preview->full upgrade, revisit, OCR, Describe. Highest value on archives/SMB (expensive bytes()), near-free on FsSource (OS page cache). RAM-only, dropped on nav/Esc (privacy #2, same category as pending_uploads). Decide scope (archive-only vs all) + byte budget. Behind a seam + A/B via PB_PERF resize numbers.

subtasks.title: Break down the 7s open->first-photo (it is NOT a full unzip)
subtasks.description: CORRECTION: a ZIP is already lazy - open reads only the central directory + a local header per entry (ZipSource::open), then bytes(i) inflates ONE entry on demand. It is 7z that is eager (whole archive -> RAM on open, because solid). So the 7s is NOT unzip-everything; it is ~all the 39MB single-entry read over SMB + ~0.3s decode. Sub-instrument metric 1 into phases (open-cmd -> worker/central-dir done -> first bytes() read -> first decode -> present) to confirm the read dominates. NB a ZIP is not background_open (kind.rs:50) so open runs sync on the event loop; verify that is not itself a stall.

subtasks.title: Thumbnails: keep a tiny window warm when parked (bounded, off by default cost)
subtasks.description: Owner call: do NOT always-capture everything (thumbs are off by default; bad trade for never-users). Happy medium: keep capture off by default, but when PARKED (held_nav is none), derive thumbs for a tiny window - current + next 2-3 - off-thread on the existing derive thread. Those items are already decoded/resident, so it is pure downsample (tens of ms each), zero source reads. Result: opening the panel always shows the neighbors instantly + rest fill on scroll, instead of a wall of placeholders for seconds. Blaze pays nothing (parked-gate); RAM capped (handful). Today thumbs_capture (app_core_impl.rs:2160) is gated on thumbs.enabled which only flips on first panel open (thumbs.rs:107), so a browse-then-open re-reads all N from SMB via Job::thumb. The ring-reuse (GPU-downsample a resident VRAM texture) stays a fallback for evicted items.

subtasks.title: First-image priority / bandwidth on a slow source
subtasks.description: The prefetch already ranks the on-screen photo tier-1 (request_prefetch sharpen/head), but on a slow source its full-res read competes for bandwidth with the whole window's preview reads. Explore throttling concurrent reads from an archive/slow source so the first image isn't fighting its neighbors. Separable from the byte cache; only pursue if #2 shows read-bandwidth contention (vs a fixed open cost).

subtasks.title: Preview-first for big JPEGs via the embedded EXIF thumbnail
subtasks.description: The real fix for the 7s first-photo over SMB. Large JPEGs embed a small thumbnail near the file start (owner test file: JPEGInterchangeFormat 240, len 22467 = 22KB). We already have pb_decode::exif_thumbnail but only use it for the thumbs strip; the main viewer decodes the full JPEG and shows nothing until done. Read just the first ~128KB of the entry, pull the embedded thumb, show it in ~100ms (blurry, fit-to-screen), then read the full entry in the background and upgrade to sharp (the preview-first model RAW/HEIC already use). Needs (a) a partial entry read - bytes() reads the whole entry today; (b) a JPEG preview-first path in decode. Turns 7s of placeholder into instant-preview->sharpen.

subtasks.title: Resize: jump to true 1:1 SIZE instantly (upscale the fit texture), then sharpen
subtasks.description: Owner-observed two-stage Fit->1:1: (1) a small grow to an intermediate size, (2) ~1s spinner, (3) a jump to true pixel-1:1. Cause: in Fit mode finalize (common.rs:84) downscales the texture to the fit box (true res kept only as orig_width/orig_height), and ViewTransform base_scale for Original is 1.0 = draw the bound texture at 1:1 of ITS dims (view.rs:110). So the toggle shows the low-res fit texture at 1:1-of-reduced-dims (near fit size, wrong) until the full-res re-decode lands and present_slot re-places at the true dims (the big jump). Fix: on the toggle, place the quad at the TRUE size using orig_width/orig_height and let the GPU upscale the fit texture - so you jump to the correct SIZE instantly (soft), then only sharpness improves when the full decode arrives. One soft->sharp transition, no intermediate size step. The resize twin of #106.5 (EXIF preview-first); pairs with #106.1 (byte cache) so the sharpen is not gated on an SMB re-read.

subtasks.title: Hold the full-res of the PARKED photo so 1:1/zoom is instant (the real zoom win)
subtasks.description:
MEASUREMENT (warm, PB_PERF): reads are ~37ms/33-38MB (OS SMB cache warm - the 7s first-photo was the ONE-TIME cold read); steady-state the DECODE (~300-500ms per 36MP JPEG) is the whole cost. Every Fit<->1:1 toggle bumps the geometry epoch and re-decodes the WHOLE ring at the new fit (log: items 0-7 re-decode around each resize). Root cause (owner, confirmed): decode-to-fit only caches the fit-sized texture and discards the full-res (true res kept only as orig_width/orig_height, common.rs:84), so 1:1 re-decodes every time - even toggling back and forth.

DESIGN (owner, 2026-07-17): while BLAZING keep decode-to-fit (small, the prime directive). When PARKED, background-decode + HOLD the full-res for a small SEQUENTIAL window - current + previous + next (radius 1, 3 items) by default; NOT the random-deck neighbors. Then Fit<->1:1<->Fit on the current photo (and on an immediate neighbor after one nav) are instant REBINDS - decode paid once, in the background, never on the toggle. Serve BOTH modes from the full-res (GPU downscales for Fit, 1:1 for Original). Drop full-res outside the window on nav.

CONFIGURABLE + OOM-SAFE (owner: easy to dial in; constrained systems must be able to reduce it): a Settings knob for the full-res cache radius - 0 = current only (or off), 1 = current+/-1 (default), maybe up to a small cap. VRAM math: 36MP RGBA8 ~= 144MB each, so radius 1 = ~432MB of full-res on top of the fit ring; bound it against a VRAM budget and let a slow box dial to 0. Random-deck neighbors are a possible later addition (owner may want after real use), left out for now. REPRIORITIZES: #106.1 byte-cache is a COLD/SMB win (nothing for a warm resize); THIS is the actual zoom win.

tasks.title: Copy: one honest "Copy" that copies whatever makes sense (pixels and/or the file)
tasks.description: Owner's insight 2026-07-17: "on the mac, don't you kind of get both?" Both platforms' clipboards are multi-representation, so offer every representation that makes sense and let the TARGET pick - Photoshop takes the pixels, Explorer takes the file. *** SCOPE WARNING: most of this is ALREADY BUILT - verify before planning. *** (1) The two-format copy SHIPS: clipboard.rs's module doc already argues this rationale; Windows writes CF_DIBV5 + CF_HDROP together (win::set takes path: Option<&Path>), macOS writes .tiff + .fileURL on one NSPasteboardItem (CoreModel.swift:3216). (2) The label is half-converged: macOS's menu bar ALREADY says "Copy" (MenuBar.swift:293); only menu.rs:1269 (Windows) and CoreModel.swift:1111 (the macOS context menu) still say "Copy Image". (3) A door ALREADY copies its file - source.path(item) is a real path, so CF_HDROP is already offered and you can paste an archive into Explorer today. REAL REMAINING WORK: (a) relabel "Copy Image" -> "Copy" in the two places above; (b) don't offer an image when there isn't one - on a door, skip the decode and emit a ClipboardPayload::File { path } arm (Windows drops the DIB from win::set; macOS's `if let tiff` is already conditional so it just skips); (c) LINUX WRINKLE: arboard has no file-list support, so set_image_and_file there already ignores the path and copies pixels only - a file-only payload would land NOTHING, so fall back to the path as text. WHY ONE GENERIC LABEL: muda has no menuNeedsUpdate, so per-item relabelling means a menu rebuild per item ON THE BLAZE PATH (the rebuild-on-signature pattern used by the subtitle flyout). "Copy" needs no rebuild and is never a lie. NON-GOAL (owner, 2026-07-17): a Copy Filename command. Copy File Path copies the full path and the owner says that's the main use case and the more useful of the two. Separate commit from #105 (touches both shells, improves photos too), but it's an afternoon.

tasks.title: Harden the deck-open pipeline against cross-type races (deferred follow-ups)
tasks.description:
Follow-ups from the Codex root-cause review of the 'archive door card frozen over a photo' bug (fixed 2026-07-17 by a core-side extend guard in apply_scan_batch + a winit shell cross-cancel of the folder-scan and archive-open workers). The primary bug (mode A: a stale folder-scan batch extending an archive deck) is fixed on BOTH shells by the core guard. These are the remaining, lower-severity hardening items Codex recommended:
(1) macOS shell (pb-mac-ffi) parity: mirror the winit begin_archive_open/begin_dir_scan cross-cancel so starting either worker drops the other. Without it, macOS is still exposed to 'mode B' (a stale folder scan's FIRST batch bootstrapping over an archive opened just after the scan started) - LOW severity (a clean rebuild onto the wrong-but-valid folder deck, not the frozen-view corruption; the core guard already covers mode A on mac). Needs an on-device build to verify (cfg(macos), can't compile on Windows).
(2) Shared open generation (Codex #1/#2): replace the global scan_bootstrapped boolean + independent archive_gen/scan_gen with ONE monotonic open generation shared by both worker types, threaded through the contract (BeginArchiveOpen/BeginDirScan effects + ArchiveResolved/ScanBatch events carry it), so any result whose generation != the latest open is dropped in the core - the general, race-proof fix that also closes mode B shell-neutrally.
(3) Decode identity (Codex #4): add content_gen/deck_gen to DecodeKey and its dedup identity, and check both epoch AND content generation on every outcome (decode_pool.rs / drain_results). Epoch is geometry identity; it should not carry deck identity alone, or a cross-deck stale decode can dedup as current.
(4) Renderer upload correctness (Codex #5): make Renderer::upload_slot return bool/Result; only call ring.mark_resident after a successful upload, and check mark_resident's currently-ignored return (ring.rs reports a stale reservation). Make an out-of-bounds upload a loud error, not a silent return.
(5) present_item result propagation (Codex #6): make present_item return success and have try_present_target/drain_results propagate it; on a genuine present_slot miss, abort the current drain batch and resync ONCE after the loop (never invalidate mid-loop - that was the reverted cff70ca0/c383107a repair that bumped the epoch mid drain_results and purged the retained full-res tier, regressing instant fullscreen to a preview flash).
Codex full analysis saved during the 2026-07-17 session. The present_slot->bool signature + the PB_DOOR_DIAG diagnostics (render draw-source + core door belief + present_slot-miss log) are already in the tree from that session and are the starting point for (4)/(5).

tasks.title: Stuck preview: full-res never upgrades in the normal flow (blurry in Fit / tiny in 1:1)
tasks.description:
Owner-reported 2026-07-18, reproduces on a plain SSD FOLDER too (so NOT archive-specific; an archive only widens the timing window). Sometimes loading a photo shows the low-res EXIF preview and it NEVER sharpens until a resize / fullscreen toggle / scale change forces a fresh decode. The unifying clue: pressing 0 (1:1/Original mode) in that state SHRINKS the image to the PREVIEW's native size — proving both symptoms are ONE root: the full-resolution decode is stuck at the preview stage (preview shown; full upgrade never completes). In Fit mode → upscaled/blurry; in Original mode → the tiny preview at true 1:1. A resize re-decodes fresh and completes.
NOT the surface-drop bug (the preview IS presented; it's the full that's missing) — distinct from the frozen-door / same-size-Lost surface issue (that one still needs surface recreation, held in reserve).
Candidate mechanisms traced (app_core_impl.rs, verify with a diagnostic — DON'T guess): sharpen_now (~5653) only requests the full while display_slot(d).is_some() && preview_resident.contains(d) && !upgrade_done.contains(d); request_prefetch (~5497) SKIPS the sharpen when `resident && !is_prev` ('already full'). So a preview that's resident-but-not-in-preview_resident, or shown via the single-image path (load_current_sync ~6814 uses set_image, outside the ring, so display_slot is None), or a full outcome dropped in drain_results' retain (~6611: kept only if `is_prev && !img.is_preview`; else dropped and possibly upgrade_done'd) — any of these leaves the preview stranded. Cancellation is cleanly discarded (decode_pool ~388/417), so it's NOT that. upgrade_done (~6471/6611) is the permanent 'stop sharpening' flag — a genuine decode error OR a full-that-came-back-a-preview sets it.
NEXT: add a gated preview->full lifecycle diagnostic (preview presented / sharpen requested / full landed: is_preview, is_prev, kept|dropped|upgrade_done) so ONE capture pins which path strands it, then fix. Likely a pre-existing #106.5/#106.7 interaction, not the recent mip/resize work.
